newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Metrobank 96 net profit over 5.0 bln pesos.
newsitem.headline: Metrobank 96 net profit over 5.0 bln pesos.

text.p: Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co (Metrobank) posted a net profit in 1996 of a "little over" 5.0 billion pesos, up from 3.5 billion pesos in 1995, a bank official told Reuters on Wednesday.
The bank had aimed for a net income target of 5.0 billion pesos in 1996.

The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said the bank had actually earned a higher figure in 1996 but it set aside a higher loan provision for doubtful accounts than what was normally required by the Central Bank.

For this year, the bank had set a net income goal of 7.0 billion pesos, of which 6.5 billion could be coming from its banking operations and 500 million from its units and affiliates, the official said.
The bank, the largest in the country in terms of capital, will start the year with a 33 billion-peso capitalisation and will hope to end 1997 with 40 billion pesos.
"With 33 billion pesos, there is enough elbow room for the bank (to meet its targets)," the official said.
The bank will open 35 branches this year from its current network of 335, he said.
Overseas, the bank will start two full-service branches in 1997 - one in Taiwan, its fourth in the country, and another in Seoul, the first Philippine bank to do so, he said.
The official said the two percentage-point cut in reserve requirements, scheduled to be completed by July, would free more funds for the bank to meet rising loan demand.
"It would all be used up. We will be lending in bulk without sacrificing quality," he said.
The official added the bank will continue with its strategy in investing about 10 to 15 percent in non-banking joint ventures.
